settings.title: the material you can build — and understand — by hand
settings.lede: Grown on six continents. Shaped with hand tools. Tested in university labs. Bamboo is the frame material you can actually understand — and understanding is what makes it sustainable.

settings.title: strong where it counts
settings.body: Tensile strength comparable to mild steel — tested to BS ISO 22157 at Swansea — with flax-and-carbon joints. It gives over the bumps and stays stiff under power, so it moves with you.
settings.quote: Independent engineers fatigue-modelled a bamboo frame to outlast around 26 times its intended service life.

settings.headline: understanding is the real sustainability
settings.body: the greenest material is the one you understand.
settings.footnote: understand what bamboo is, how it grows and how it's joined, and you use it better — you waste less, repair instead of replace, and keep improving. that's why everything we do is teaching.

settings.quote: We don't ask you to take "bamboo is good" on faith. We test it, we teach it, and we work with universities to understand it better.

settings.heading: the research behind bamboo
settings.lede: We don't just build with bamboo — we study it, and we teach it. A decade of testing, student projects and peer-reviewed research.

settings.heading: how bamboo measures up
settings.lede: A frame material comes down to how light it is, how strong for that weight, how it soaks up the road, and whether you can build it yourself. Honest ranges, with sources.
settings.tile4_lbl: A skill you keep for life
settings.notes: Ranges reflect species, alloy and lay-up — bamboo especially varies with species, culm and moisture, which is exactly why we test to a standard. Our 84 MPa is a real culm section tested at Swansea (BS ISO 22157). † Carbon's headline strength is measured along the fibre; a frame tube only ever sees a fraction of it. Sources: Swansea University test data; Sharma & Harries (2015); Wegst & Ashby (2004); MatWeb / ASM.
settings.framing: Carbon is lighter and stiffer. Bamboo answers on damping and comfort — and it's the only one of the four you can build yourself, by hand, in a weekend.

settings.heading: any design. any rider.
settings.lede: You can't shape steel in your kitchen or cut carbon in your garage. Bamboo you cut with a hand saw and join with wrapping and epoxy — so you can build any frame you can draw.

settings.question: How strong is a bamboo frame?
settings.answer: Comparable to mild steel in tension — about 84 MPa, tested to BS ISO 22157 at Swansea University — while far lighter. Every joint is reinforced with a flax-and-carbon composite, so in our builds the bamboo is the limiting factor, not the joins, and independent engineers have fatigue-modelled bamboo frames well beyond their service life (Arango Fierro et al., 2019).

settings.question: Does it crack, or mind the rain?
settings.answer: Our tubes are heat-treated and sealed with epoxy resin. Dry after wet rides and store indoors — the same care you'd give any quality frame.

settings.question: Do I need experience to build one?
settings.answer: No — most of our builders start with none. Workshop frames are completed in 2 days with full expert guidance; home kits include step-by-step instructions and video tutorials.

settings.question: How long will a bamboo frame last?
settings.answer: Many of our 2012 frames are still ridden daily, 14 years on. Keep it sealed and stored indoors and it goes the distance.

settings.question: What types of bamboo bicycle can I build?
settings.answer: Any type — road, gravel, mountain, cargo, tandem, balance bike. The geometry is defined by your jig setup, so the design is up to you.

settings.question: Is bamboo a sustainable material for bicycles?
settings.answer: Yes. It matures in 3–5 years (trees take 20–50), regrows from its root system, and needs no pesticides or irrigation. And because you build the frame yourself, you learn to repair it — so it lasts for years rather than being thrown away.
